findings.title: [P1] Restore tenant validation before granting document reads
findings.body: When `userTenant !== documentTenant`, `canReadDocument` now returns `true`, allowing cross-tenant access. This replaces the existing tenant-equality authorization check with unconditional approval and exposes documents outside the caller's tenant.

findings.title: [P1] Restore tenant equality validation before granting document reads
findings.body:
`canReadDocument` now authorizes every request. Any user whose `userTenant` differs from a document’s `documentTenant` can read that cross-tenant document, breaking tenant isolation and exposing protected data.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restore tenant isolation in `canReadDocument`
findings.body:
Returning `true` authorizes every read regardless of tenant. Any call with `userTenant !== documentTenant` now permits cross-tenant document access, bypassing the function’s authorization boundary.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
